description: Four UI templates over the same contract. Scores are 1-5; buildEffort is low/medium/high. The mockups are annotated SVG wireframes, not screenshots.

templates.name: Pocket Log
templates.summary: History-first phone app. Keeps the shipped flow — History as home, Start workout, the workout below the strip — but restyles the controls and proposes four bottom destinations.
templates.fidelity: Every shipped surface has a home; chrome is a proposal. Literal current screens are kept as shipped references.
bestFor: existing users and their muscle memory
strengths: No new interaction model to learn
Matches the current data flow exactly
risks: Still five content areas competing for attention
Week status is a small strip, easy to miss
The workout still lives inside the Log tab rather than being a mode
proposed: week status on the log screen

templates.name: Workbench
templates.summary: Catalog rail, dense editable session in the middle, and a persistent dock for rest, week status and last time. Keyboard-first.
templates.entry: Open a session from the rail
screens: nutrition and groceries as reading panels
templates.fidelity: Full training workflow; content becomes secondary reading.
bestFor: logging at a desk or on a tablet
reviewing a whole session at once
power users who correct numbers often
strengths: Whole session visible without scrolling on a laptop
Rest timer and last-time numbers never leave the screen
Fastest correction of a mistyped set
risks: Poor fit for a phone at the rack
Dense table needs care for screen readers
Nutrition and program content feel like an appendix

templates.name: Focus
templates.summary: A workout mode, not a destination. One exercise fills the screen, sets are large steppers, and rest owns the bottom edge.
templates.fidelity: Logging only. History, progress, content and backup live outside the mode.
bestFor: mid-set, one hand, chalk or gloves
pairing with any of the other templates
strengths: Rest timer is impossible to miss
No navigation decisions during a workout
risks: No overview of the whole session
Steppers need a type fallback for odd numbers
Cannot browse or edit a template mid-workout

templates.name: Dashboard
templates.summary: Review-first. The week is the home screen: completion ring, four-week consistency grid, one-line strength trend, next session and nutrition targets.
templates.fidelity: Adherence and trends first; detailed entry is reduced to one tap into another template.
bestFor: sharing progress without opening a log
strengths: Answers 'how am I doing?' in one screen
Consistency grid makes missed weeks obvious
risks: Needs enough history before it looks useful
Trend cards can mislead if only one session exists

comparison.note: Scores are design judgements, not measurements.

recommendation.why: Pocket Log keeps every current surface and reuses the existing rules, so it can ship first. Focus is a low-effort workout mode that any template can enter. Workbench is the same components laid out for a wide screen, not a separate rewrite.
recommendation.deferWhy: Dashboard is a different product bet: it optimises for adherence rather than entry. Build it once the log is stable and there are a few weeks of data.
recommendation.ifYouMustPickOne: workbench for a tablet-at-home lifter; pocket-log for a phone-at-the-gym lifter.
